added_failures_note: The reviewed run's manifest carries no baseline_suite arm: its done_when and the plan section both assign the importer-population base arm to the coordinator at merge, and the node was told not to run one, so only the after arm exists. The head arm is logs/gate-test_figure_review.log, whose summary line reads '7 passed in 33.58s' with EXIT=0 - zero failing test ids, so no id can be absent from the base and added by the head. The count is therefore a measured zero from the head arm, not an assumed one; no base log was read because none was run.

assertion_analysis.failure_condition: No assertion is added by this diff; three are removed (the parser assertions at old lines 307-314). The retained assertion 'assert item in prompt' is independent of anything the test passes in: FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS is read from the module under test and the prompt text is loaded from reckon/crew/prompts/figure_review.md, so reinstating the regression - removing one FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS entry from the prompt - reddens it. Observed in logs/negative-control.log: removing the data_ink bullet made it fail with "assert 'data_ink' in ..." (1 failed, EXIT=1), and the prompt was restored, which I verified by diffing 93d61013e..df3946ee5 for reckon/crew/prompts/ (no change) and by the clean worktree at df3946ee5. The brief assertions at tests/test_figure_review.py:296-306 compare composed brief text against literal phrases, so they too are independent of the code under test.

No assertion guards the deletion itself: nothing in tests/ fails if parse_figure_review or _FIGURE_RUBRIC_LINE_RE is reintroduced. Re-adding either symbol leaves the suite green, so the removal is held by review only. That is the durability gap recorded against this node; it is not a defect in the landed behaviour, since the deleted parser had no production caller.

findings.text: follow-on: the node's declared negative control mutates a path outside its four declared write paths. The source prompt declares 'remove one FIGURE_REVIEW_ITEMS entry from reckon/crew/prompts/figure_review.md', and the control log proves the mutation was applied - its captured prompt text is missing the data_ink bullet - so the red log that admits this node was produced by a write the node's write grant (reckon/crew/review.py, tests/test_figure_review.py, the fragment, figures dir) does not cover. I verified the file was restored: the reviewed worktree is clean at df3946ee5 and git diff 93d61013e..df3946ee5 shows no change under reckon/crew/prompts/, so no stray edit landed. It matters because a control whose mutation file is outside the grant makes the fence unenforceable as written, and a reader can only tell a restored control from a stray edit by diffing the tree rather than by reading the record.
